source_policy: SEER Cancer Stat Facts, ACS Cancer Facts & Figures 2026, USPSTF. Citable; refresh yearly. NCCN not used.

incidence.us_annual_new_cases: ~333,830 projected for 2026 — the leading cancer diagnosis in men
incidence.rank_among_cancers: Most common cancer in men; ~15.8% of all new cancer cases
incidence.trend: Incidence rising ~2.9%/yr, including notable rise in regional/distant-stage disease — a concerning shift attributed in part to screening changes

mortality.five_year_survival_overall: ~98% (relative), among the highest of major cancers
mortality.trend: ~69.5% diagnosed at local stage; very high survival overall but markedly lower in distant disease

risk_factors.detail: Most frequently diagnosed at 65-74; rare before 40
Higher incidence and mortality in non-Hispanic Black men
First-degree family history; germline BRCA2 and other HRR/Lynch alterations raise risk and aggressiveness

modalities: MRI and biomarker reflex in evolving pathways
screening.guideline_summary: USPSTF recommends individualized shared decision-making on PSA screening for men 55-69 (grade C), and against routine PSA screening at 70+. Earlier discussion for higher-risk groups. Cite USPSTF; NCCN not used.
screening.notes: PSA screening involves a documented benefit-harm tradeoff (overdiagnosis of indolent disease); active surveillance is standard for low-risk disease

epidemiology.presentation: Usually asymptomatic and screen-detected; advanced disease may cause urinary symptoms or bone pain
